findings.description: The bucket omits any ACL/public access block and is documented as public, allowing anonymous read (and potentially write) of its contents, which include a customer master data file.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to this internet-exposed bucket leaves no audit trail for detecting unauthorized reads.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects deleted or overwritten (maliciously or accidentally) cannot be recovered; combined with force_destroy = true this permits irreversible data destruction.
A file named customer-master.xlsx is uploaded into the publicly accessible, unencrypted aws_s3_bucket.data, exposing sensitive customer records to anonymous internet users.
The financials bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for the financials bucket, leaving no audit trail of access to sensitive financial data.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so financial objects can be overwritten or deleted without any recovery path.
The operations bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest by configuration.
No logging block is configured, so access requests to this bucket are not recorded for audit or incident investigation.
The data science bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so its data is not encrypted at rest by default.
The central log bucket does not configure its own access logging, so tampering with or exfiltration of audit logs would go unrecorded.
